cachedJobs.title: Frontend Developer
cachedJobs.description:
About the Role

We are looking for a Frontend Developer who combines strong web fundamentals with solid problem-solving skills to build clean, responsive, accessible, and high-performance user interfaces. You will work closely with designers and backend developers in an Agile team.

Responsibilities
Build responsive web pages using semantic HTML5, CSS3 (Flexbox, Grid), and SASS
Develop interactive features in JavaScript (ES6+) such as form validation, modals, and dynamic filtering
Write reusable, modular code by applying OOP principles and design patterns
Optimize application performance (lazy loading, debouncing, image and CSS optimization) and improve Lighthouse scores
Ensure cross-browser compatibility (Chrome, Firefox, Safari) and accessibility (WCAG)
Integrate REST APIs using the Fetch API and Async/Await
Translate Figma designs into pixel-perfect UI
Participate in code reviews, pull requests, and Agile ceremonies
Required Skills
B.Tech/B.E. in Computer Science or a related field (2025 graduates preferred)
Strong command of HTML5, CSS3, Flexbox, CSS Grid, and Responsive Design
Proficiency in JavaScript ES6+: closures, promises, async/await, event loop, DOM manipulation, prototypes
Good understanding of Data Structures & Algorithms and time/space complexity
Solid knowledge of OOPs concepts, SOLID principles, and design patterns (Singleton, Observer)
Experience with Git, GitHub, VS Code, Chrome DevTools, Postman, and npm
Familiarity with Figma and Local Storage
Good to Have
Problem-solving profile on LeetCode, GeeksforGeeks, or HackerRank
Knowledge of Java or C++
Hackathon participation or mentoring experience
Personal projects or portfolio showcasing UI work
What We Offer
Mentorship from senior engineers and a clear growth path
Exposure to performance-focused, accessible, and scalable UI development

questions.question: What is a closure in JavaScript?
questions.reference_answer: A closure is a function that remembers and can access variables from its outer scope even after the outer function has finished executing.

questions.question: How did you reduce search response time from 400 ms to 150 ms?
questions.reference_answer: I used hash maps for O(1) lookups and debouncing to avoid firing the search on every keystroke.

questions.question: What is the difference between Flexbox and CSS Grid?
questions.reference_answer: Flexbox lays out items in one dimension (row or column), while Grid handles two-dimensional layouts (rows and columns together).

questions.question: How does the JavaScript event loop work?
questions.reference_answer: The event loop moves queued callbacks (microtasks first, then macrotasks) onto the call stack whenever the stack is empty, enabling non-blocking async behavior.

questions.question: How did you raise your Lighthouse score from 68 to 92?
questions.reference_answer: By compressing images, adding lazy loading, and minifying CSS to cut load time and render-blocking resources.

questions.question: What is the Observer design pattern and where would you use it?
questions.reference_answer: It lets multiple subscribers get notified automatically when a subject’s state changes, such as in event listeners or state-update systems.

cachedJobs.title: Cloud Infrastructure & DevOps Engineer
cachedJobs.description:
We are seeking an experienced Cloud Infrastructure & DevOps Engineer to design, deploy, and automate robust multi-region AWS cloud architectures. Key responsibilities include orchestrating Docker containers with Kubernetes (EKS), managing Infrastructure as Code with Terraform, designing automated CI/CD deployment pipelines, and ensuring security and compliance for financial systems.

Required Skills:
- AWS Cloud Services (EC2, S3, IAM, VPC, RDS)
- Kubernetes & Docker containerization
- Terraform / Infrastructure as Code
- CI/CD (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI)
- Python / Bash automation scripting
- Linux system internals & networking

questions.question: Describe the architecture of a highly available, multi-AZ Kubernetes cluster on AWS (EKS) and how you manage stateful workloads.
questions.reference_answer: Deploy control plane across multiple AZs managed by AWS EKS, worker node groups in private subnets across 3 AZs with ALB ingress controller, and EBS CSI / EFS CSI drivers with persistent volumes for stateful workloads.

questions.question: Explain how you implement Infrastructure as Code (IaC) with Terraform for automated blue-green deployments.
questions.reference_answer: Use remote S3 state backend with DynamoDB locking, modular VPC and ECS/EKS resource definitions, and switch traffic between blue and green target groups via Route 53 or ALB listener rules.
